business_problem: Volkswagen Group needed a standardized, resilient way to connect order intake, logistics, and manufacturing across its global factory network so it could deploy AI and production IT systems at scale, reduce the risk of line stoppages, improve quality control, and support faster rollout of new vehicle models and future software-defined vehicle processes.
solution_summary: Volkswagen Group uses its Digital Production Platform (DPP), described as the company's "factory cloud," together with AWS cloud infrastructure and machine learning services to standardize digital manufacturing across global plants. The DPP acts as the orchestration and data backbone, linking order intake, logistics, and manufacturing so data remains continuously available across the process chain. Production-critical applications such as Guided Vehicle Completion are rolled out uniformly through the platform, while AWS provides the scalable cloud environment that hosts these systems. Volkswagen also uses Amazon SageMaker to train AI models for industrial computer vision and other manufacturing use cases. Specific AI applications include KI4UPS for assisting assembly teams with in-factory vehicle software deployment, real-time image analysis for quality assurance, predictive maintenance, remote monitoring, and plant-level energy optimization. Together, the shared data foundation, cloud-hosted systems, and AI services let Volkswagen operationalize AI across plants while preparing manufacturing for software-defined vehicles.

data_flow: Data from order intake, logistics, and factory operations is connected through the Digital Production Platform, which provides a shared data foundation across plants. Cloud-hosted production systems on AWS use that flow to run standardized applications, while Amazon SageMaker-trained models power computer vision, software-deployment assistance, predictive maintenance, remote monitoring, and energy-optimization use cases consumed by assembly and quality teams.
